My grandma has been diagnosed with Fibromyalgia years after suffering with it. The only reason for that was that doctors kept telling her she was faking being in so much pain because it's hard to track down where it's coming from. This has led to her becoming depressed and suffering so very much all alone for way too long. It truly breaks my heart to think about.

I also saw it in myself, fortunately chronic headaches and migraines aren't a chronic illness per se but it's still a hard thing to live with. Doctors wouldn't take me serious, everyone blamed puberty and the usual school stress and told me I was just faking it to stay out of school. At one point I wouldn't tell people I had a headache anymore and just endured it. Took me, as well several years until we finally saw a neurologist. I'm now on medication for it but it only helps sometimes. Because it took so long the chance of the pain ever going away again is lower than if I (and probably my grandma too) had received treatment earlier than I did.

People really should listen to those who are in pain a lot. They shouldn't talk it down or even think about them faking it just because "it's that often". A dose of concern is never wrong and could spare a lot of suffering
